freeze_note: The v1 30-qubit capacity candidate completed on one A800 during development calibration. Version 2 freezes the calibrated 33-qubit candidate before any release-eligible rerun; earlier development measurements remain ineligible. Version 2 carries four amendments. First, the single-device capacity failure is read as provenance evidence rather than as a release-gate payload, so world size 1 is no longer a required release world; the measured bar is unchanged, see capacity_workload.single_gpu_baseline.rationale. Second, the release structure is written down. The matched-speed workload is deliberately smaller than the capacity workload, because a ratio needs a baseline that one device can actually run; every matched-speed release payload therefore states the single_gpu_expected_oom of the capacity premise it rests on and names that premise in capacity_premise_workload_sha256, and such a payload is not a claim that the timed workload itself needs more than one device. Third, the frozen timing protocol is repointed to benchmarks/manifests/statevector_speed_workload_v2.json. The method is unchanged - the same warmup and measured iteration counts, the same diagonal of three perturbation points, the same timed unit - and only the size of those points changed, because the v1 sizes would have needed roughly 6.6 h for the baseline leg alone and so could not have been run as frozen alongside the multi-node legs the same manifest requires. Fourth, the multi-node requirement is answered by two pair legs at world size 8 with four ranks on each host: a matched-speed leg, which is the only way the released speedup is measured across a real host boundary, and the capacity completion leg the capacity workload requires. The single-node worlds and the pair world therefore measure the same protocol, and every pair payload reports node_count 2 with the route it observed.

topologies.note: single_node_world_sizes names the world sizes the gate requires among the promoted release worlds; each is measured in this campaign as a single-node leg of the matched-speed protocol, so the same world size 8 is also measured across the two hosts. The multi-node requirement is answered by the pair legs, whose payloads report node_count 2 and an observed InfiniBand route.

single_gpu_baseline.rationale: A single device cannot shard one logical workload across ranks, so no world_size=1 artifact can satisfy the release gate: a true scalability claim is rejected by 'sharded_across_ranks requires world_size > 1', and a false claim by 'release gate requires scalability_claim_allowed=True'. Requiring world size 1 among the release worlds was therefore unsatisfiable, not a measured bar. The single-device capacity failure is still mandatory, still signed, and still required to report the frozen capacity digest; it is read as provenance for the capacity requirement it demonstrates, excluded from the release worlds, and excluded from the per-rank release payload field contract, which asks for rank communication and per-rank gradients that one device has no ranks to report. It is also read from results_path rather than from benchmarks/results/scalability, because the strict promotion audit requires every file in that directory to be release-grade sharded scalability evidence, which a single-device run can never be.
